questions.question: What does an explicit planning stage add to an agent system?
options: Nothing useful — planning is purely decorative
Breaking a complex goal into an ordered set of sub-tasks before or during execution, giving a scaffold to check progress against
It replaces the need for any tool use entirely
It guarantees the agent will never make mistakes
questions.explanation: Planning breaks a large goal into ordered sub-tasks, giving both the agent and observers a structure to track progress against, rather than operating purely reactively with no sense of the overall goal's structure.

questions.question: What is the key difference between 'upfront planning' and 'plan-and-execute'?
options: They are identical approaches with different names
Upfront planning generates the full plan once before execution and doesn't adjust it; plan-and-execute re-evaluates the plan after each sub-task based on new information
Plan-and-execute never uses any planning at all
Upfront planning is always more expensive than plan-and-execute
questions.explanation: Upfront planning commits to a fixed plan before execution begins, while plan-and-execute re-evaluates the remaining plan after each step, making it more adaptive at the cost of additional re-evaluation overhead.

questions.question: An agent tasked with a multi-part research and reporting goal gets sidetracked and never completes the final report. Which question best diagnoses this?
options: Should we conclude the underlying model is simply not capable enough?
Does this agent generate an explicit plan and track progress against it, or does it operate purely reactively without a structure to catch it wandering off-goal?
Should we increase the model's temperature to fix this?
Is this an unfixable limitation of all AI agents?
questions.explanation: This is a classic symptom of an agent operating without an explicit plan and progress tracking — adding a planning stage (and monitoring progress against it) is the standard, addressable fix for an agent wandering off the actual goal.
